newsitem.title: USA: Dallas Fed's McTeer - U.S. economy "running hot".
newsitem.headline: Dallas Fed's McTeer - U.S. economy "running hot".

text.p: Dallas Federal Reserve President Robert McTeer Thursday said the U.S. economy was "running hot" and there was no indication that the expected slowdown had begun as yet.
In remarks to a business group, McTeer also made clear that the price indicators he watches showed little troublesome inflation.
"The numbers that are coming in seem to be delaying that cooling off period just a little bit," he said, adding "so it is running hot, the pedal is to the metal."
Speaking later with reporters, McTeer said there was a risk that the benign inflation picture could worsen.
"There is a risk it will pick up," he said. "So far we have been either smart or lucky."
But he said that risk would fall if growth were to return to a more moderate level with inflation perhaps staying below three percent.
He also made clear that the Consumer Price Index overstated prices levels by 1/2 to perhaps 1-1/2 percent.
"I think many people are using one percent as a rule of thumb," he said.
During his remarks and in answer to questions, McTeer said that the United States suffers from a very low savings rate, and that efforts must be continued to reduce the budget deficit.
"If we had more incentive for savings, the financial incentives for more investment would follow fairly automatically," he said.
He said the "most direct" thing you could do to increase national savings would be to cut the budget deficit.
